Susan M. Collins

Republican candidate for U.S. Senator, Maine · Incumbent

U.S. Senator from Maine (incumbent)

Susan Collins is the Republican U.S. Senator from Maine. She was first elected in 1996 and took office in 1997. She won the 2026 Republican primary and is running for reelection against Democratic nominee Troy Jackson in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Collins stands

Russia sanctions
Called on President Trump to reverse his waiver of Russian sanctions and his diesel deal (said at an October 2026 campaign event in Lewiston).
One Big Beautiful Bill / Trump-backed legislation
In a debate with Troy Jackson, defended her support for Trump-backed legislation, including the One Big Beautiful Bill.
Campaign finance
In the WMTW debate, denied reports that she received illegal campaign contributions. Also denied Jackson's claim that she profited from the Iran war.
Campaign advertising
Her campaign said some attack ads in the Maine Senate race have gone too far.

Background

  • U.S. Senator from Maine, 1997–present (first elected 1996)
  • Born December 7, 1952, in Caribou, Aroostook County, Maine
  • Won the 2026 Republican primary for U.S. Senate in Maine
